title.en: Path, time scaling and joint limits

summary: Separate the geometric path from the schedule along it, so speed limits change timing without changing the path.
objective: Build a joint-space path with a time scaling I can change, showing velocity and acceleration profiles against declared joint limits.
intent_signals: Show the difference between a path and a trajectory.
Change how fast a robot follows the same path without changing the path.
example_prompts: Build a joint-space straight-line path with an adjustable time scaling and limit checking.
Show velocity and acceleration profiles for the same path under two different time scalings.
negative_signals: Not a collision-free motion planner: obstacle avoidance is out of scope.
Not a torque-level controller; actuator dynamics are not modelled.
not_for: Not a collision-free motion planner: obstacle avoidance is out of scope.
Not a torque-level controller; actuator dynamics are not modelled.

entities.name: Path definition
entities.guidance: Define the path in joint space between start and end configurations with the path parameter visible, since the scaling acts on that parameter.

entities.name: Time scaling profile
entities.guidance: Plot the scaling and its derivatives in the scene so the schedule is an object rather than a hidden curve.

entities.name: Limit check
entities.guidance: Compare peak joint velocity and acceleration with declared limits and report which joint binds.

state_contract.model: Authored planar 2R display arm with lengths 2 m and 1 m and unrestricted revolute joints. FK: p=(2 cos(q1)+cos(q1+q2),2 sin(q1)+sin(q1+q2)) m. Stored unwrapped joint endpoints define q(s)=q_start+Deltaq s without shortest-angle wrapping; defaults (0,0) to (pi/2,pi/2). For finite T>0 and u=t/T in [0,1], cubic s=3u^2-2u^3, s_dot=(6u-6u^2)/T, s_double_dot=(6-12u)/T^2. Trapezoid chooses authored acceleration duration tb=T/4, peak v=4/(3T), a=16/(3T^2): for 0<=t<tb, s=a t^2/2 and s_dot=a t; for tb<=t<T-tb, s=v(t-tb/2) and s_dot=v; for T-tb<=t<=T, s=1-a(T-t)^2/2 and s_dot=a(T-t). Accelerations are respectively a,0,-a with one-sided values at switches. Hold endpoints outside [0,T] with zero speed/acceleration and label acceleration jumps. q_dot=Deltaq s_dot and q_double_dot=Deltaq s_double_dot. Per-joint limits default to 1 rad/s and 2 rad/s^2, editable finite positive values. Exact peak magnitudes are |Deltaq| times 1.5/T and 6/T^2 for cubic, or 4/(3T) and 16/(3T^2) for trapezoid; report violations, never clip the path.
state_contract.authority: The path and the scaling are separate authoritative objects; changing the scaling must never change the geometric path traced by the end effector.
actions: Switch between the cubic and trapezoidal time scalings.
Play, pause and scrub the trajectory.

invariants: The end-effector path is identical under every time scaling of the same joint-space path.
The scaling starts at zero and ends at one, so start and end configurations are reached exactly.
A violated joint limit is reported with the joint named, rather than being clipped silently.
The supplied formulas give analytic peak bounds for these schedules; any separately sampled peak estimate is labeled and never substitutes for those bounds.
motion_guidance: Evaluate the analytic schedule at the requested scene time for playback and scrubbing; stored samples may cache those evaluations but their interpolation is labeled approximate.
Show the profile cursor moving together with the arm, so timing and pose are linked visually.
known_limits: Kinematic scheduling only: real limits also come from torque, payload and thermal constraints.
The stated schedules have acceleration jumps and no jerk limit. Display sampling changes only the rendered approximation; it does not redefine the analytic joint path or its peak bounds.
Authored guidance only: no scene runtime, rendering or numerical calibration has been run for this recipe.

claims.statement: A robot configuration as a function of time is a trajectory, while a path is a curve in configuration space parameterised by a path parameter running from zero to one, and a path becomes a trajectory by defining a time scaling that maps the time range onto that parameter range.
claims.scope: Definitions as cited; the simplest joint-space path is the straight line between start and end configurations.

source_refs.locator: 9.1 and 9.2 Part 1, path, trajectory and time scaling definitions

claims.statement: Common time scalings include a cubic polynomial whose velocity is parabolic and whose acceleration is linear, a fifth-order polynomial that additionally sets zero acceleration at both endpoints, a trapezoidal profile of constant acceleration, constant-velocity coast and constant deceleration to rest, and a seven-segment S-curve with constant-jerk phases; the actual speed and acceleration also depend on the path distance and total duration, not only on the form of the scaling.
claims.scope: Named families and their qualitative derivative structure as presented in the cited section; specific coefficient formulas were not transcribed from that page and must be derived from the endpoint conditions the scene declares.

source_refs.locator: 9.1 and 9.2 Part 2, cubic, quintic, trapezoidal and S-curve time scalings

object_craft.structure: A visible trace of the end-effector positions along the path with markers at the sampled path parameter values.
object_craft.material: Neutral trace material with a distinct marker for start and end so the path is legible at rest.
object_craft.articulation: The trace is regenerated only when the path endpoints change, never when the scaling changes.

object_craft.structure: Plot rails in the scene carrying scaling, velocity and acceleration curves with a shared time axis.
object_craft.material: Opaque plot plates with gridlines and units so peaks can be read against the limit lines.
object_craft.articulation: A cursor moves along all three plots together during playback.

physical_contract.scope: Analytic kinematic scheduling and optional cached playback; no dynamics, contact or hardware feasibility certification.
checks: The traced path is unchanged when the scaling changes.
Scrubbing to a time reproduces the same joint state every time.
